title: Opportunity-Cost-Throughput (OCT) Prioritization Model for Runtime & Console Roadmap
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Introduce a complementary prioritization framework (Opportunity-Cost-Throughput, OCT) to augment RICE for features that trade off per-token cost, latency tail behavior, and throughput predictability. OCT focuses on quantifying the opportunity cost of capacity and supply constraints for runtime and console investments.
background: Existing RICE-based playbooks surface reach and confidence well, but they underweight operational economics for serving (batching, KV cache hit rate, quantization impact). Several recent roadmap debates (dedicated autoscaler tuning, prefix caching UI, kernel selection telemetry) highlighted the need for a scoring model that explicitly accounts for capacity opportunity cost and throughput elasticity.
problem_statement: Product decisions are being made with inconsistent signal about how much a given investment will free up capacity or reduce unit cost under realistic traffic distributions. This causes oscillation between investing in feature velocity vs investing in cost-of-ops improvements with longer-term ROI.
proposal_summary: Adopt OCT as a lightweight scoring sheet to be used alongside RICE. OCT produces two outputs: (1) a normalized Opportunity Cost score capturing the tokens-hours freed or reallocated, and (2) a Throughput Elasticity multiplier describing how changes scale across typical request distributions. Combine OCT with RICE by treating OCT Opportunity as a modifier to Impact and Cost in RICE for final ranking.
scoring_components: Opportunity Cost: estimated token-hours saved per week (normalized 0-10). Throughput Elasticity: how % throughput changes with the change (normalized 0-3 multiplier). Risk/Confidence: engineering confidence in the estimate (0-1). Implementation Cost: dev+infra effort (story points, used as divisor).
scoring_formula: OCT_Score = (Normalized_Opportunity_Cost * Throughput_Elasticity * Risk_Adjustment) / (1 + Implementation_Cost/10). Final_Priority_Score = RICE_Score * (1 + OCT_Score/10).
example_calculation: Example: Prefix KV cache UI feature: estimated token-hours saved = 60k token-hours/week -> Normalized_Opportunity_Cost=7. Throughput_Elasticity=1.4. Risk_Adjustment=0.85. Implementation_Cost=13. OCT_Score=(7*1.4*0.85)/(1+1.3)=6.625/2.3=2.88. If RICE_Score=50 then Final_Priority_Score=50*(1+2.88/10)=50*1.288=64.4 -> boosts priority for capacity-improving work.
implementation_notes:
- Add OCT fields to the roadmap spreadsheet template and product planning doc.
- Run a 4-week pilot: apply OCT to next three cycles of runtime & console candidates.
- Collect real post-launch metrics (token-hours, burst rejection rates) to calibrate normalization buckets.
- Provide a short workshop for PM/Eng leads on estimating Opportunity Cost and Throughput Elasticity.
- Instrument a tagging convention in JIRA/Linear linking features to baseline telemetry queries (e.g., KV cache hit delta, average batch size).
acceptance_criteria: 1) OCT scoring column present in the planning spreadsheet and PRD template. 2) At least 8 candidate features scored with OCT in the pilot cycle. 3) Two prioritization sessions run with Eng + Infra discussing OCT-derived changes. 4) Calibration report with recommended normalization buckets published to Confluence.
comments: 2025-11-16 - Initial draft by Liam. Raised during roadmap offsite. Asked Eng leads for typical telemetry slices.
2025-11-20 - Feedback from Runtime Eng (Noah Kim): want clearer guidance on estimating throughput elasticity; suggested three example archetypes (latency-sensitive, batch-friendly, KV-bound).
2025-12-01 - Design input (Marisa Chen): asked to include UX cost (support burden) as a small modifier to Implementation_Cost for console changes.

2026-01-12 - Finance review (Priya Rao): proposed converting normalized opportunity cost to $/week buckets for an alternate view linked to billing impact. We're keeping token-hours primary for engineering alignment but adding a $ view as optional column.
2026-02-05 - Pilot kickoff: added 10 candidate features from runtime and console. Assigned worksheet owners. Workshop scheduled for 2026-02-12.

2026-03-10 - Interim calibration: early pilot results show KV cache improvements have higher realized Opportunity Cost than estimated for low-latency tail workload; adjusting normalization for KV-bound archetype upward by one bucket.
